verbalization: Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin is indicated for Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) with Npm1 or Cebpa somatic mutations, and it is also associated with AML with Inv3(p21;q26.2) or T(3;3)(p21;q26.2). This relationship is supported by a shared pathway involving Idarubicin, which is indicated for all three conditions. The mechanism of action for Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin is primarily through the binding of its monoclonal antibody to the CD33 antigen on the surface of AML cells, followed by the intracellular activation of the enzyme phospholipase C-γ, which leads to the production of inositol trisphosphate and subsequent calcium release. This process induces apoptosis in the leukemic cells. The presence of Inv3(p21;q26.2) or T(3;3)(p21;q26.2) mutations is associated with a more aggressive form of AML, and the use of Idarubicin, which is a topoisomerase II inhibitor, may enhance the efficacy of Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin in these cases. The evidence suggests that the drug's mechanism of action is relevant to the pathophysiology of AML with these specific mutations, though the exact role of the mutations in the drug's efficacy remains to be fully elucidated.
